reader.notes: The grammar makes integer-2 an unsigned integer literal, so 'at least one' comes down to 'not zero'. IntegerOperandPass refuses zero in every PAGE phrase at every edition. A negative value cannot be written, and an omitted HEADING defaults to 1.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: pghneg (HEADING -1) and pghpos (HEADING +1) give COBOL0001 'unexpected -'/'unexpected +', exit 65. pgh00 (HEADING 000) gives COBOL2386 'shall be nonzero', citing §1985:III.2, exit 65. pghdec (HEADING 1.0) gives COBOL5506 'only an integer literal is expected', exit 65. pgnolim (PAGE HEADING 3 FIRST DETAIL 2, with no integer-1, a 2023 form) gives COBOL5506 'expected ARE, IS, LIMIT, LIMITS or an integer literal', exit 65. So no written integer-2 below one reaches the program, and the omitted phrase defaults to 1 (BindReportDescriptionClauses GR3a, matching OK §1985:XIII.3.8.4 GR2). OK §1985:XIII.3.8.3 SR3 'Integer-2 must be greater than or equal to one'; OK §1985:III.2 'must be neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed'.
